claims.text: Adding approximately 1–3 at.% carbon during synthesis will induce in situ formation of coherent nanoscale carbide precipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
A controlled nanoscale dispersion of carbide precipitates produced by carbon addition will enhance yield strength.
A controlled nanoscale dispersion of carbide precipitates produced by carbon addition will enhance ductility.
Uniform carbon distribution and controlled cooling can favor coherent nanoprecipitates over coarse or heterogeneous phases.
High-purity synthesis will avoid extraneous impurities.
The intervention will produce uniformly distributed, coherent nanoscale carbide precipitates embedded in the alloy matrix.
The carbide nanoprecipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
The nanoprecipitates will strengthen the alloy through Orowan strengthening.
The coherent precipitates will provide sites for dislocation nucleation.
The coherent precipitates will promote strain hardening.
Precipitate-induced strain hardening will delay necking.
Relative to the carbon-free baseline alloy, the carbon-doped alloy will have increased yield strength.
Relative to the carbon-free baseline alloy, the carbon-doped alloy will have increased plastic strain to failure.
The beneficial effect requires a fine, homogeneous precipitate distribution.
Excessive carbon or suboptimal processing may produce coarse precipitates or unwanted phases that harm the strength–plasticity combination.
